title: Foundations: Gospel Quartet - The Complete Guide
summary: What Gospel Quartet is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Gospel Quartet songs: Gospel quartet singing is four voices in tight harmony — lead, tenor, baritone, bass — trading verses over minimal accompaniment. Born in jubilee traditions, it became the sound of groups like the Soul Stirrers.

History: Jubilee quartets toured colleges in the 1870s–1900s. The Soul Stirrers (with Sam Cooke), the Swan Silvertones, and the Dixie Hummingbirds electrified quartet gospel in the 1940s–50s; Cooke carried it into soul music.

How the songs work: Gospel Quartet favors the keys of G, C, F, Bb. Common forms include Verse trading: each singer takes a verse; Tag ending repeated until the spirit says stop. Players should master bass singer walking under the harmony first, then lead singer improvising over the group's bed. Guitar or piano support; voices lead.
